active_leaf.result: Within the tested repository-transport scope, a Chat-native effect was successfully gated on exact readback of a prior CAS checkpoint. The prepared state was exact-read back as blob 3808a5376adee298606612094f50d6f589fb8d05 before the effect was issued; the resulting role-local effect was then exact-read back as blob ce2dd15e654e0901e77080c6ab6ac5f3a4a83916. This proves ordered readback-before-effect for this one GitHub repository effect, not atomic exactly-once delivery for arbitrary external systems.

evidence.observation: GitHub's create-or-update contents endpoint requires the current blob SHA when updating a file and documents conflict responses; serial repository mutations are required for conflicting content operations.
evidence.scope: Repository-content CAS-like transport semantics only; this does not prove atomicity with arbitrary external systems.

evidence.tested_scope: one role-local GitHub repository contents effect
the demonstrated readback-gated repository effect chain
evidence.qualification: Repository API transport can be rate-limited, but no monthly/trial/paid quota or external compute path is required by the tested mechanism; transient transport limits are cross-invocation recovery conditions.

substantive_claims_added.claim: For one role-local GitHub repository effect, scheduled Chat can enforce the ordering checkpoint-CAS -> exact checkpoint readback -> effect issuance -> exact effect readback without richer-mode/protected/manual execution and without finite monthly/trial/paid quota or incremental monetary cost.
substantive_claims_added.scope: Only the tested repository-contents transport chain; no claim of atomicity or exactly-once semantics for arbitrary non-repository side effects.
